author: blu
body: The reference test reads CODE lines only. Testing the whole file marked a cite used when the citing chapter merely mentioned a name in its column-2 prose, which is the same defect shape as a checker a comment held green: the thing being searched was not the thing that constitutes use. Prose lines carry exactly one leading space and code carries two or more, so the split is mechanical; the cite lines are dropped too, since a cite names a chapter and a chapter can share a name with a definition.

author: blu
body: A sum type's constructors are indented under it behind a bar, so neither the definition nor the type pattern above reaches them and Just and None were invisible to this lint. That was masked for as long as the cite line itself was searched: `cites Foreword chapter Maybe` contains "Maybe", which IS extracted, so any chapter sharing its name with a type it declares could never be reported unused whatever its body did.
